Add subtle animated ocean waves to the page background. No libraries, CSS and inline SVG only. Do not change the layout, colors of the cards, or any game features.

1. Put 2 or 3 layered wave shapes along the bottom of the page (about the bottom 15 to 20% of the screen), behind all content. Use the existing navy and teal palette at low opacity (around 0.08 to 0.15) so they never compete with the text or cards. Keep the waves the same colors on every screen and every difficulty.
2. Animate them slowly sideways at different speeds (about 15 to 30 seconds per loop) so they gently roll, looping seamlessly with no jump.
3. Add a few small bubbles that slowly float up along the left and right edges only, away from the main content, also at low opacity.
4. Make everything position: fixed, z-index behind the content, with pointer-events: none so nothing blocks clicks or the fish cursor.
5. Respect prefers-reduced-motion: if the user has reduced motion on, show the waves but don't animate them.
6. On phones under 900px, keep the waves but remove the side bubbles.

Check every screen (home, mission, play, end) at 1920x1080, 1366x768, and 375px phone width to make sure text stays readable. Commit with "Add animated wave background" and push to Abigail_Front_End_Work.
</pasted_content id="f7cf">

content.text:
The page now has an animated wave background. I committed it as "Add animated wave background" (`ea5f815`) and pushed it to `Abigail_Front_End_Work`. I checked all four screens at the three sizes and the text stays readable everywhere.

**What I added** (`public/index.html` and `public/style.css`; no layout, card or game code changed):
- **Waves:** three layers along the bottom, made from inline SVG. The back layer is teal at 0.08 opacity and slides left every 30s. The middle layer is navy at 0.15 and slides right every 22s. The front layer is teal at 0.10 and slides left every 16s. Each wave is drawn as two identical copies side by side and slides by one copy's width, so the loop has no jump. The colors are the same on every screen and difficulty.
- **Bubbles:** six small bubbles, three along each side edge, float up at about 0.14 opacity. They're named `bg-bubble` so they don't clash with the fish cursor's `fish-bubble`.
- **Behind everything:** the background is `position: fixed`, sits behind the content with `z-index: -1`, and has `pointer-events: none`. The element at the bottom of the screen is the page itself, not the waves, so the waves don't block clicks or the fish cursor.
- **Reduced motion:** the waves still show but don't move. I also hid the bubbles in this mode, because they'd otherwise sit there as stray dots. Say if you'd rather keep them visible and still.
- **Under 900px:** waves only, no bubbles.

**How I tested it:** the Chrome extension wasn't connected, and `npm start` failed because the packages aren't installed. So I served `public/` locally, ran headless Chrome, and played a full medium run at 1920×1080, 1366×768 and 375px. The game used its built-in sample messages because the server wasn't running. The page never scrolls sideways at any size.

Between 900px and about 1200px, the content fills almost the whole width, so the edge bubbles pass behind the cards there. They're faint and behind the cards, so they don't affect anything.

The screenshots are in `C:\Users\black\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\1da4ec57c02c3532\d6a5387c-baa9-4adb-99a2-4e173ecb231f\scratchpad\shots` if you want to look.

7. Add 2 small schools of tiny fish (3 to 5 simple fish shapes each, inline SVG) that slowly swim across the background near the waves, one going left and one going right, about 25 to 40 seconds per pass. Make them very faint (opacity around 0.1 to 0.15) and a muted blue-gray, not teal, so they don't look like the fish cursor. Show them ONLY on the home screen. Remove them as soon as the player leaves the home screen, and show them again if they come back to it. Same rules as the waves: behind all content, pointer-events: none, no animation with prefers-reduced-motion, and hidden on phones under 900px.

content.text: All behaviors check out. Let me look at the fish themselves.

I added two faint schools of fish to the home screen background. They behave as you asked, but I haven't committed them yet.

**What they look like:** one school of 4 fish swims right in 34 seconds, and one school of 5 swims left in 27 seconds. Both sit just above the waves, bob gently up and down, use the muted blue-gray (`#9fb7c9`) at 0.12 opacity, and are clearly different from the teal fish cursor.

**Home screen only:** they're switched off by the same screen marker the page already uses to hide the big header. When you come back to home, they start swimming again. I didn't need to touch any game code.

**Same rules as the waves:** they're in the same layer behind all content, with `pointer-events: none`, and are hidden under 900px.

**Reduced motion:** the fish stay on screen but don't move. They sit still near the left and right edges, because their normal starting point is off-screen.

**What I checked** (in headless Chrome, with the game's sample messages):

| Size | Home | Mission | End | Back to home |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920×1080 | visible and moving | hidden | hidden | visible again |
| 1366×768 | visible and moving | hidden | hidden | visible again |
| 375px | hidden | hidden | hidden | hidden |

With reduced motion on, both schools show and stand still.

The changes are in `public/index.html` and `public/style.css`. Do you want me to commit and push them to `Abigail_Front_End_Work`?
